## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by tan to brownish wings with translucent pale patches, dark speckling, and spotted or checkered markings that give it a delicate patterned appearance. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, roadsides, wetlands, disturbed areas, and other open habitats where low herbaceous host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on plants in the amaranth family, including pigweeds, beets, and related greens, often webbing or tying leaves together as they feed.
